raw_response:
I farm only 7 mu, so I can't take big risks. What I do this year is mostly the same wheat-maize rotation as always, because that keeps grain coming and spreads the risk. I only finished one season not long ago, so I remember clearly where the wheat did well and where the maize got weak when the rain was short. People around me also do wheat first, then maize right after harvest, so I will follow that timing. I have well water, so if the sky stays dry I can still save the crop, but pumping costs money, so I won't water too many times unless the field really needs it.

For wheat, I still want a steady stand going into winter, so I will sow in early October with a common improved variety sold locally. I usually put most fertilizer before sowing and then add some urea at jointing if the leaves look light. I don't dare cut fertilizer too much, because if wheat turns yellow the yield drops fast, but I also can't spend freely. For maize, the turnaround after wheat is tight, so I will harvest wheat and plant maize within a few days, with simple rotary tillage and quick sowing. Maize grows fast in summer, so I will give it a base dressing and one topdress, then irrigate only if rain is not enough. Herbicide is necessary for both crops, and if insects show up in maize I will spray once. I mainly depend on family labor, with little hired help.
